newsitem.title: NORWAY: Oslo Bourse in final talks on new trading system.
newsitem.headline: Oslo Bourse in final talks on new trading system.

text.p: The Norwegian stock exchange said on Friday it had entered final negotiations with an Australian supplier on a new computer system for trading in equities.
The Oslo Bourse has in the last few months evaluated two proposals of a new trading system -- one being the SBF Paris Bourse and the other Computer-share Systems Limited (CSL) of Australia.

"After an overall evaluation of technical and functional solutions, the Oslo Stock Exchange has decided to enter final contract negotiations with Computershare Systems Limited for a new equity trading system," the bourse said in a statement.
"The Swedish IT supplier CMA will be contract partner and system integrator. CSL will be the supplier of the trading system ASTS: Automated Securities Trading System," it said.
The new system is scheduled to be in production by 1998.

The bourse originally had planned to have a new trading system in place in 1996, but in March last year it cancelled a 51 million crown contract with Logica Plc for the system because of alleged delays caused by the British software company.
The new electronic trading system will provide users with an automatch system, as opposed to the current system where orders are matched manually by phone.
Decentralised, off-floor trade will allow for overseas brokers to become members of the Oslo Bourse, one of the smallest in Europe.
